# Preface {.unnumbered}

**This is a publishing scaffold, not a published or accepted engineering textbook.**

The intended book develops first-principles coherent receiver theory and practical design methods for experienced RF engineers. Its provisional chapter organization is recorded in the accepted planning package under ADR-0004; technical development remains subject to review.

The opening technical unit develops physical representations and conversion signs
through a continuous two-channel phase comparison. It is a provisional draft,
not the complete planned Chapter 1.

The next bounded teaching units develop scalar stochastic phase reasoning,
observation-weighted coherence, and covariance/quadratic forms. They connect
dependence and circular quantities to finite observation and coupled error models.
Phase/delay inference then separates local precision from ambiguity; model
adequacy tests sensitivity and numerical reasoning before acquisition/tracking
examines wanted-signal retention. These developing foundations retain provisional
status and do not complete their planned chapters.

[Fields, geometry and physical transduction](fields-geometry-transduction.qmd)
then connects incident fields to loaded receiver voltages and shows what electronic
injection cannot establish. [Physical disturbances](physical-disturbance-paths.qmd)
constructs noise and interference from sources and their actual transfer paths.
[Extraction, integration and rejection](extraction-integration-rejection.qmd)
uses those responses and disturbances to calculate detection outcomes and retained
wanted information. Each bounded unit includes a worked receiver decision, a
misleading alternative and a changed-assumption exercise. Their diagrams and
calculations describe supplied models; they do not establish hardware behavior
or complete the planned chapters.

The opening requirement framing now leads to an exercised
[frequency, phase and delay plan](frequency-phase-delay-transfer.qmd), with
conversion orientation, unwanted bands and state-sensitive references. The
[architecture and allocation treatment](feasibility-architecture-allocations.qmd)
then intersects headroom, information, time and resource limits before refining
them through physically constructed correlations and environmental paths.
A model can reject a proposed operating point or expose a missing interface;
passing its equations does not demonstrate a realizable receiver.

[Analog information preservation](analog-information-preservation.qmd) then
turns the selected signal/blocker envelope into filtering, gain, nonlinear
response and history-dependent validity decisions.
[Synthesis and endpoint distribution](synthesis-endpoint-references.qmd) derives
loop choices and reference noise, spur, loading and environmental obligations.
[Distributed timing and carrier inference](distributed-reference-inference.qmd)
separates remote epoch, rate, phase, path ambiguity and evidence age. Their
worked calculations compare conditional alternatives and identify the component,
calibration and operating-state evidence needed before hardware decisions.

[Sampling and converter feasibility](sampling-converter-feasibility.qmd) then
reconciles the admitted analog waveform with rate, driver, clock, quantization
and recovery limits. Its declared alternate lower-side frequency plan preserves
the earlier conversion signs without replacing the original high-side design.
[Quadrature and conjugate-response fidelity](quadrature-conjugate-fidelity.qmd)
uses identified training to preserve both frequency signs and genuine near-DC
information, then challenges the correction with changed level and state.
[Multirate processing and finite resources](multirate-finite-resources.qmd)
realizes a bounded NCO, filter, decimator and fractional resampler with explicit
sample epochs, words, state and transport obligations. Its numerical comparisons
start from the same converter words; they cannot repair previously lost analog
information. A remote resampler uses a separately established clock relation;
aligned baseband samples do not by themselves establish RF phase coherence.

[Complex-response alignment](complex-response-alignment.qmd) then chooses a
common delayed response subject to causality, finite support, word range and
noise gain before combination. Its deep-attenuation and true-null cases show
when a different observation or architecture is required.
[Calibration observability and operational metrology](calibration-observability-metrology.qmd),
placed earlier in Chapter 13, establishes what a test can distinguish and how
loading, reference correlation, finite records and coherent floors affect its
conclusion. [Calibration procedures and continued coherence](calibration-procedures-coherence.qmd)
uses that access and uncertainty with feasible correction, independent wanted-
signal checks and a maintenance policy that accounts for evidence age and downtime.

The progression is from a defined observable through conditional source/path
budgets and subsystem interfaces to executed processing, correction and measurement
examples. It supports rejection of infeasible alternatives and identifies the
component, platform and physical evidence needed before hardware decisions.
These examples do not supply a reconciled, validated complete receiver. Actual
real-time hardware closure, complete transition and environmental realization,
whole-system qualification and specialist/reader evidence remain outstanding.

Bounded canonical treatments now occupy Chapters 1–20, including the measurement
reasoning in Chapter 13, and the calibration treatment in Chapter 23. Chapters
21 and 22 remain explicitly reserved for state integration and physical/environmental
engineering. Their slots preserve the accepted chapter destinations; supplied
contracts in the developed examples do not complete those missing methods or
any entire planned chapter. The publishing demonstration and relative-phase pilot
are grouped as **development supplements**. Their temporary rendered numbers after
Chapter 23 do not supply later canonical treatments.

The publishing demonstration tests mathematics, references, SVG figures and bibliography wiring. The following dual-channel relative-phase pilot develops a bounded illustrative engineering argument and supporting calculations. It has no hardware measurements, specialist acceptance or actual reader-trial evidence.
